question.text: Reinvestment risk in bonds refers to:

answer.text: The risk that the bond issuer will default
The risk that coupon payments cannot be reinvested at the same rate assumed in YTM calculations
The risk that inflation will erode returns

explanation.text: The Logic: Reinvestment risk is the risk that intermediate cash flows from a bond cannot be reinvested at the same rate as promised or desired. YTM assumes coupons are reinvested at the YTM itself; when market rates fall, coupons get reinvested at lower rates and realised return falls below YTM. Zero-coupon bonds have no reinvestment risk because there are no periodic coupon payments. The Trap: Option A describes default (credit) risk. Option C describes inflation risk. Option D describes currency risk. Reinvestment risk is specifically about the rate at which coupon cash flows can be redeployed.
